text:
sam: quick sanity check — we're seeing ~12% higher p99 latency on GCP a100s compared to AWS for the same SKU + driver combo (CUDA 11.8 / nvidia-driver 525.x). anyone else hit this?

mia: yup saw that on the nightly onboarding run for redwood-l2-quant. throughput flat, but tail jumps on longer sequences. cc @raj for perf artifacts. :thinking_face: 

raj: I pulled the run logs: https://internal.redwood/charts/bench/1769 — looks like kernel fallback counts are higher on GCP, also temps slightly elevated. not sure if throttling.

alex: charts look different by region too — us-west1 vs us-west-2. attaching quick png: https://internal.redwood/assets/1769/p99-vs-seq.png (small).

perf-bot: nightly-run summary: model=redwood-l2-quant, batch=8, seq=2048, gpu=a100-80gb, cloud=GCP/AWS, p50/p90/p99: AWS 45/82/160 ms, GCP 47/85/180 ms. reg=+12% p99 GCP vs AWS.

toni: could be kernel selection (cublas/cuBLASLt) or numa memcpy paths. can we run microbench: cublas gemm, cudnn conv, and single-thread memcpy to compare?

mia: agree — also want to rule out driver patchlevel. GCP images sometimes ship with a slightly different nvidia package. raj, can you ssh and dump `nvidia-smi -q` + `modinfo nvidia`?

raj: done, pasted snippets below:
```
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name,memory.total --format=csv
Driver Version: 525.85.12, Name: NVIDIA A100-80GB, Memory Total: 81184 MiB
```
`modinfo nvidia | grep -E "version|parm"` shows vendor packaging tags: gcp-patch-02.

alex: that packaging tag might explain kernel differences. also noticed GCP nodes had governor set to "ondemand" vs AWS set to "performance" on boot scripts. that would affect sustained throughput for long sequences.

sam: good catch. can someone run this command for a quick parity check across clouds?
```
bench-runner --model redwood-l2-quant --gpu a100 --seq 1024 --batch 8 --runs 20 --cuda 11.8 --driver 525.85 --collect-kernel-stats
```
put results in /tmp/bench-176921 and link here.

raj: kicking off now in us-west1, us-west-2, eu-west1. will post short table.

perf-bot: microbench scheduled: cublas-gtx, cudnn-conv, memcpy-uni for all targets. ETA ~18m.

mia: also flagging potential quality regression from quantization: if we hit different kernels we might see small output drift — please add a quick eval diff (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-cos) to the job.

raj: results uploaded: https://internal.redwood/artifacts/176921/quick-parity.csv — quick summary inlined:
- AWS us-west-2: p99 158ms, memcpy 3.2GB/s, cublas-gemm peak consistent.
- GCP us-west1: p99 178ms, memcpy 2.6GB/s, occasional kernel fallback count=4 per run.
- EU-west1: p99 162ms, memcpy 3.0GB/s.

toni: kernel fallback is key clue. sounds like GELU/SiLU fused kernel not picked on GCP image. can we force kernel selection override to validate?

alex: also worth checking CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES ordering + MIG defaults — sometimes driver bundles change device indexing which impacts our NUMA probe.

sam: action items: 1) validate driver packaging difference with infra (raj), 2) run forced kernel selection test (toni), 3) run eval diff to catch quant quality drift (mia). if GCP still worse after those, open infra ticket for image rebuild.

infra-bot: created INF-2028: Investigate GCP packaging + default governor (linked to bench artifacts). Assigned to @raj.

mia: I'll add the eval diffs to the bench-runner job and re-run nightly. posting results here when done. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks team — this thread helps a lot. if you find a quick workaround (governor toggle or kernel hint), drop the config in ops/benching/README so dedicated runs can pick it up.

alex: noting for capacity planning: if GCP p99 is persistently higher we'd size extra 10% headroom for dedicated pools in that region. add to the sizing doc.

raj: will follow up with a short write-up once INF-2028 has findings.

sam: ack, closing out for now but will re-open if perf persists. :eyes:
